analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (lines 462-1261) plus the partial patch excerpt. This is an offline CI workflow-structure test file. It does not touch provider runtime code, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), key custody, or the encrypted prefix-cache implementation (T-041). No production control is changed. The base-side tests assert fail-closed CI properties: parity steps are not continue-on-error; cache saves happen only on master/dev pushes (SAVE_CACHES); fixture caches are keyed by manifest hash with no restore-keys; checkouts use persist-credentials: false; and the test-provider job contains no secrets, coordinator or platform references. The patch excerpt hardens VALIDATE_GIT, so a restored .git cache is discarded if it contains symlinks, hooks, fsmonitor/hooksPath/include config, or fails fsck. That is a CI supply-chain improvement and not a regression. The excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), and the head-side lines were not supplied as numbered text. I therefore could not independently check the new CACHE_GATE and Darkbloom-cache logic (changed head ranges 152-215, 1089-1118, 1335-1407) or the surrounding workflow YAML. The actual workflow files, such as provider-tests.yml, the composite action and the scripts the tests read, are not in this batch. Open integration questions: whether the workflow YAML matches the loosened or tightened assertions, and whether the new Darkbloom Sandbox cache gate keeps untrusted cache content from reaching privileged jobs. No concrete security finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
